pages.title: Dossiers
pages._note: The dossier is Filinq's unit of municipal work — folder batches run on it, the legal-bases summary reports on it — and until 2026-09-07 it had a schema, a spec and a controller but NO surface: a user could not create or open one anywhere in the app. type:custom rather than type:index because the row context (document count as home-folder ∪ documents[], resolved legal-basis chips, lifecycle status) is aggregated by DossierManagementController, not readable from a plain OR index.

pages.title: Dossier
pages._note: Aggregates documents, legal bases, anonymisation runs and publication state. Selecting a document swaps the inline viewer through store state, never a route push, so switching causes no reload. Every dossier-level action calls the endpoint that already owns it — nothing here reimplements batch, report or publication logic.

pages.title: Contracts
pages._note: contract-lifecycle-management REQ-DDCLM-006: OpenRegister lists the documentContract objects directly (its RBAC decides who sees them: filinq-contract-managers and admins); a row opens ContractDetail through rowRoute, because the detail is a custom page, not type:detail. Create and edit are the object API's own dialog; status starts at draft and only the declared lifecycle moves it.

pages.title: Renewal pipeline
pages._note: The renewal pipeline (REQ-DDCLM-006): active contracts bucketed in the browser (src/services/contractPipeline.js) into expired, notice due within 30 days, ending within 90 days and later, from the objects the caller can read; renew and end on every row. MUST stay declared BEFORE /contracts/:id: vue-router matches in declaration order, so the :id route would swallow /contracts/pipeline.

pages.title: Contract
pages._note: One contract (REQ-DDCLM-001/002/004/005): terms, parties named from their contacts (GET api/contracts/{id}/parties), documents (attach from Files, generate from a template through api/documents/generate), send for signature (an ordinary signing request, recorded through POST api/contracts/{id}/signing, which also links the signed document back once the request completed), suggested terms with accept and reject, and put in force, renew and end.
